radiology_report:
Radiology Division | Amsterdam UMC VUmc | 05 Jan 2025 | Exam: multiparametric MRI prostate

Clinical indication:
Assessment of an elevated serum prostate-specific antigen level (8.6 ng/mL) alongside clinical concern for malignancy.

FINDINGS:
Glandular measurements indicate a total volume of 26.9 mL. T2-weighted sequences reveal an 8 mm focus of intermediate signal intensity located within the right mid-gland peripheral zone. Diffusion-weighted imaging shows mild restriction without significant ADC hypointensity. Dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences demonstrate an absence of definite early focal enhancement. There is no evidence of extraprostatic extension, seminal vesicle invasion, or suspicious pelvic lymphadenopathy.

IMPRESSION:
Focal lesion in the right mid-gland peripheral zone consistent with PI-RADS 3.
Prostate volume 26.9 mL; PSA density 0.32 ng/mL/mL.
csPCa predicted probability 0.8191391

previous_notes.author: Dr. N. Kuiper (GP)
previous_notes.text: Clinical review documented a persistent elevation in prostate-specific antigen levels. Initial testing in March 2024 recorded a value of 7.2 ng/mL, with subsequent assays demonstrating a continued climb to 8.6 ng/mL. The free-to-total PSA ratio remains suppressed at 10%, and the calculated velocity reaches 2.45 ng/mL per annum. These consistent numerical increases prompted further urological assessment via multiparametric MRI.
